title: Closure compactification realizes the immersion adjoint and its bounds
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $s:S\hookrightarrow T$ be an immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, factored as $s=v\circ c$ with $c:S\hookrightarrow V$ closed and $v:V\hookrightarrow T$ open [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the two small sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Put $F_\tau=v_{\tau,!}c_{\tau,*}$ and $J_\tau=Rc_\tau^!v_\tau^*$ for $\tau=e,p$, with the pasted adjunctions $F_\tau\dashv J_\tau$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient, lem-exc-proetale-closed-support, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], where the two open extensions are those of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Let $\bar S$ be the scheme-theoretic closure of $s$, with $s=i\circ u$, $u:S\hookrightarrow\bar S$ open and $i:\bar S\hookrightarrow T$ closed [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Here $\bar S=\operatorname{SIm}(s)$ is the closed subscheme cut out by the largest quasi-coherent ideal contained in $\ker(\mathcal O_T\to s_*\mathcal O_S)$; $i$ is its image inclusion and $u$ its canonical factor map. These immersions into the Noetherian scheme $T$ are quasi-compact, so this ideal is the kernel itself. Write $E_\tau=i_{\tau,*}u_{\tau,!}$.

The schemes $T,V,S,\bar S$ are Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]; $V$ and $\bar S$ are separated and finite type over $k$, all open complements of their closed subschemes are quasi-compact, and $(u,i)$ is a compactification of the separated finite-type morphism $s$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. There is a nonnegative integer $D$ with $\dim\bar S\le D$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Both $F_\tau$ and $E_\tau$ are exact sheaf functors, whose termwise functors preserve every lower cohomological bound. The normalized sheaf identifications restricting to the identity on $S$ [lem-sfb-etale-locally-closed-extension-comparison, lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence] induce natural isomorphisms
$$q_\tau:F_\tau\xrightarrow{\sim}E_\tau$$
on unbounded derived categories. For ordinary etale compact support at $(u,i)$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] one has $Rs_!=Ri_{e,*}u_{e,!}=E_e$. If $s^\times$ denotes its ambient right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], there is the canonical adjunction-conjugate identification $J_e\cong s^\times$ induced by $q_e$, preserving units and counits [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. For every $M\in D^b_c(T_e,A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], $N=v_e^*M$ lies in $D^b_c(V_e,A)$ and $H=Rc_e^!N=J_eM$ lies in $D^+(S_e,A)$. In particular the bounded-below closed direct-image comparison is defined at $H$ and at every $L\in D^+(S_e,A)$ after either open or closed extension.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a single Noetherian affine. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the given structure maps of $T$ and $S$. Thus $T$ and $S$ are Noetherian. Since $V$ is an open subscheme of $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] makes $V$ Noetherian as well. Every open subscheme of any of these three schemes is therefore quasi-compact. In particular $s,c,v$ are quasi-compact morphisms: the inverse image of an affine open is an open subscheme of their respective Noetherian source. This checks the quasi-compactness hypothesis needed for the scheme-theoretic image, rather than assuming it for an arbitrary immersion.

proof.text: Use [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] for $s$. Its image inclusion $i:\bar S\hookrightarrow T$ is closed, its canonical factor $u$ satisfies $iu=s$, and its defining ideal is the largest quasi-coherent subideal of $\ker(\mathcal O_T\to s_*\mathcal O_S)$. Since Step 1 proves $s$ quasi-compact, the same node identifies this ideal with that kernel itself. Apply [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] to the quasi-compact immersion $s$: the canonical map $u:S\to\bar S$ is a quasi-compact open immersion. Thus these are precisely the canonical maps of the statement, including any nilpotent scheme structure, rather than maps chosen only from a topological closure.

By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], $i$ and $c$ are proper, in particular separated and of finite type. The quasi-compact open immersions $v,u$ are of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], and are separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation]. Finite-type composition [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] now gives finite type over $k$ for $V$ and $\bar S$, and finite type of $s=vc=iu$. Separated composition, clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], gives separatedness over $k$ for $V$ and $\bar S$, since $T$ is separated over $k$. As $u$ is open, $i$ proper and $iu=s$, the pair $(u,i)$ is a compactification by [def-weil-compactifications-refinements].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $i:\bar S\to T$ to see that $\bar S$ is Noetherian. Every open complement in $V$ or $\bar S$ is an open subscheme of a Noetherian scheme, hence is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Finally [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] applies to the finite-type $k$-scheme $\bar S$. The chain definition of $\kundim$ in [def-kun-dimension] is exactly the topological Krull dimension in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Thus choose an integer $D\ge0$ bounding it. If $\bar S$ is empty its dimension is $-\infty$ and take $D=0$. This establishes the uniform dimension assertion without using finite-dimensionality of a general Noetherian scheme.

proof.text: On the etale site, the abelian direct images $c_{e,*},i_{e,*}$ are exact by [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction]. The constant-$A$ module direct image has the same sections and commutes with the forgetful functors to abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; module kernels are sectionwise and module cokernels are the sheafified sectionwise ones, as for abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. So forgetting scalars is exact and faithful, hence reflects exactness, and the module functors $c_{e,*},i_{e,*}$ are exact as well. The open functors $v_{e,!},u_{e,!}$ are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. On the pro-etale site, apply [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] to $c$ and $i$; their open complements are quasi-compact by Steps 1 and 4. The functors $v_{p,!},u_{p,!}$ are exact by [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. Each composite $F_\tau$ and $E_\tau$ is therefore exact: applying its two factors successively to a short exact sequence gives a short exact sequence. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] they induce termwise functors on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $\mathcal H^r(GK)\cong G\mathcal H^r(K)$ for each such exact factor or composite $G$. Consequently each preserves every lower bound, with no restriction on upper cohomology.

proof.text: On etale module sheaves, apply [lem-sfb-etale-locally-closed-extension-comparison] with $X=T$, $a=s$, $W=V$, $h=c$ and with the canonical closure $\bar S$. Its normalized identification $i_{e,*}u_{e,!}\cong v_{e,!}c_{e,*}$ has an inverse $q_e:F_e\to E_e$, still restricting to the identity on $S$. On pro-etale module sheaves, [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence] gives precisely the normalized identification $q_p:v_{p,!}c_{p,*}\cong i_{p,*}u_{p,!}$. For each immersion involved, [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] identifies the inverse image of the finite constant-$A$ ring sheaf with the specified constant ring sheaf on its source. Thus the coefficients satisfy the pulled-back-ring hypothesis of that node, including its canonical scalar maps. Apply these natural transformations in every degree of a complex. Naturality makes them chain maps and their inverses remain chain maps. Step 5 ensures that all four functors invert quasi-isomorphisms after localization; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], clause (2), descends the two isomorphisms and their inverses to the unbounded derived categories. These are the required $q_\tau$, with the specified sheaf normalization.

proof.text: Use the compactification $(u,i)$ from Step 3 in [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. It gives $Rs_!^{(u,i)}=Ri_{e,*}\,u_{e,!}$. The module sheaf functor $i_{e,*}$ is exact by Step 5 (via [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction]), so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] identifies its total right derived functor with its termwise functor on every unbounded complex. Therefore $Rs_!^{(u,i)}=i_{e,*}u_{e,!}=E_e$ under the specified canonical identifications. The hypotheses of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] hold: $S,\bar S,T$ are Noetherian, $u$ is open, $i$ is proper of finite type and $A$ is a finite commutative ring. Hence its chosen ambient right adjoint $s^\times$ is a right adjoint to this same $E_e$.

source.place: Ordinary ambient exceptional adjoint; chosen-compactification definition and Stacks derived.tex Tag 015F for exact closed direct image

proof.text:
Keep the pasted adjunction $F_e\dashv J_e$ in the hypotheses and the adjunction $E_e\dashv s^\times$ from Step 7. Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to $q_e^{-1}:E_e\to F_e$. Its conjugate is a natural isomorphism $r:J_e\to s^\times$, because conjugation sends inverse isomorphisms to inverse isomorphisms. More explicitly its Hom bijection is characterized by sending $\alpha:F_eL\to M$ to $\alpha q_{e,L}^{-1}:E_eL\to M$ before transposing under $E_e\dashv s^\times$. Denoting the two units and counits by $\eta^F,\varepsilon^F$ and $\eta^E,\varepsilon^E$, transposing the identity gives
$$r_{E_eL}\,J_e(q_{e,L})\,\eta^F_L=\eta^E_L,\qquad \varepsilon^E_M\,E_e(r_M)\,q_{e,J_eM}=\varepsilon^F_M.$$
These are exactly preservation of the units and counits under $q_e,r$, and fix the direction and normalization of the right-adjoint identification.

proof.text: Let $M\in D^b_c(T_e,A)$, and choose $a\le b$ outside which its cohomology sheaves vanish. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] the constant-coefficient inverse image $v_e^*$ is exact. The cohomology identification of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $\mathcal H^r(v_e^*M)\cong v_e^*\mathcal H^r(M)$, so it vanishes outside the same interval. For each of the finitely many relevant cohomology sheaves, intersect its finite constructible locally closed stratification with $V$. The resulting strata remain locally closed and are constructible in $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-open-restriction]. Restrict each etale cover trivializing the finite locally constant $A$-module on a stratum to its open intersection with $V$; it still trivializes the same finite module. Thus this is a finite lisse stratification on $V$, as required by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Consequently $N=v_e^*M\in D^b_c(V_e,A)$, with lower bound $a$.

proof.text: The adjunction $c_{e,*}\dashv Rc_e^!$ is the one on ordinary unbounded derived categories of [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. Its left functor is the termwise module direct image, exact by Step 5 (abelian exactness of [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction] transported through the forgetful functor), with the required localization factorization from [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Apply clause (1) of [lem-pur-exact-derived-adjunction-bounds]: $Rc_e^!$ preserves every standard lower cohomological bound. Since Step 9 gives $N\in D^{\ge a}(V_e,A)$, it follows that $H=Rc_e^!N=J_eM\in D^{\ge a}(S_e,A)\subset D^+(S_e,A)$. Only the bounded-below assertion is needed here; no constructibility claim about this value of the closed right adjoint is used.
